title: Memory-Bounded Blackboard Scheduling for Multi-Agent Workflows
research_question: Can a memory-bounded blackboard scheduler that writes only utility-ranked intermediate state to a shared workspace reduce communication cost while maintaining or improving task success in multi-agent workflows?
hypothesis: Compared with always-communicate and fixed-topology orchestration baselines, a scheduler that adaptively selects which intermediate artifacts enter a shared blackboard under a strict memory budget will improve success-per-token and latency on complex multi-agent tasks by suppressing low-value communication without removing useful coordination.
motivation: The knowledge base shows repeated rejections of ideas centered on uncertainty routing, escalation, preference-conditioned replanning, and communication gating for multi-agent workflows, indicating that this space is active but many existing proposals overlap too much. A clearer gap is budgeted shared-state management: how agents should coordinate when communication and context are scarce. This proposal shifts from generic gating or escalation to a concrete orchestration mechanism—a memory-bounded blackboard that ranks and persists only high-utility intermediate results. That makes the question falsifiable, practically relevant for LLM agent systems with context-window and cost constraints, and distinct from previously rejected workflow ideas.
